primitives.name: Thinking Out Loud
primitives.verbatim_quote: `thinking-out-loud` (skill) — ADOPT, small.** A protocol contract: act on NOTHING until an echo brief (mission, locked decisions, flips, parked tangents, model's inferences quarantined from the user's words) is approved.
primitives.assumptions: The user's initial utterance is treated as noise. Only after a formal echo brief (structured summary) is generated and approved should any action be taken.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If the echo brief fails to materialize, the system remains in a passive 'park' state, preventing premature execution.

layer2.mapping: In GSE, this maps to a state-transition guard on the input stream. When Garrett's voice dictation arrives, the system immediately enters a quarantine state. It only transitions to the active build state once a structured telemetry packet (mission, decisions, risks) is validated. This prevents confident misreads from cascading into hours of wasted computational resources.
layer2.telemetry: The primary verification metric is the rate of rejected builds due to misinterpretation of Garrett's intent. A successful implementation reduces this metric to near zero.

primitives.name: Toonify Token Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: `toonify_token_optimization` — ADAPT, tiny.** TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation): CSV-like compactness, ~64% token reduction vs JSON for tabular data.
primitives.assumptions: Tabular data (projections, actuals, slates, signals) can be losslessly compressed using TOON without sacrificing semantic fidelity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If the data contains non-tabular elements, TOON cannot be applied, reverting to standard serialization.

layer2.mapping: GSE serializes tabular projection/actuals, slate data, and signal rows as TOON instead of JSON. This reduces the payload size sent to LLMs in the backtest harness, signal intake, and Quantitative Compliance (QC) loop. The reduction in tokens per request directly lowers compute costs and speeds up response times.
layer2.telemetry: Measure the percentage reduction in API token usage when TOON is used versus JSON for typical tabular payloads. Monitor latency improvements in LLM processing pipelines.

primitives.name: RAG Failure Diagnostics Clinic
primitives.verbatim_quote: `rag_failure_diagnostics_clinic` — ADAPT, small.** Framework-agnostic P01–P12 RAG failure taxonomy + LLM triage into minimal structural fixes (~200 lines, most portable item in the repo).
primitives.assumptions: RAG failures can be categorized into a fixed set of twelve distinct classes (P01-P12). Each class has a corresponding minimal set of structural fixes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When a new failure mode emerges that doesn't match the existing taxonomy, the system may require manual intervention or an update to the diagnostic framework.

layer2.mapping: GSE adopts the RAG failure taxonomy for backtesting and pipeline diagnostics. By categorizing issues into T6 (backtest harness) and lessons-learned logs, GSE creates a shared vocabulary for diagnosing why components break. This enables the fleet to reuse fixes across incidents, improving overall reliability.
layer2.telemetry: Track the time-to-diagnosis for RAG-related errors. A well-implemented clinic reduces this time by providing a clear triage path based on the taxonomy.

primitives.name: Commit Archaeologist
primitives.verbatim_quote: `commit-archaeologist` (skill) — ADAPT, small.** Offline git-history walker reconstructing WHY code exists (origin, timeline, co-changed files, intent signals, change risk).
primitives.assumptions: The commit history is a reliable source of truth about the rationale behind code changes. Co-changed files often share a common intent.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If the commit messages are incomplete or misleading, the archaeology may lead to incorrect conclusions about the code's purpose.

layer2.mapping: GSE reimplements this as `gse-why`. Before refactoring, it is used to dig into exactly the modules that build threads touch. For example, investigating why `activeDfsSlate()` falls back to sample data. The tool surfaces any workaround or temporary markers, ensuring that refactorings do not break existing behavior.
layer2.telemetry: Monitor the accuracy of the reconstructed change histories. High accuracy ensures that developers understand the original intent correctly, reducing the risk of introducing bugs during refactoring.
